_doc: SKEPTIC cost audit (d): is the top-up's OWN cost counted? HS + freewheel switch gates, the inductor, any bias.

reference_transfer_energy_per_beat_fJ._what: what the CHAIN ITSELF spends moving charge between banks -- the yardstick

PULSED_inductor_topup.form: PULSED INDUCTOR, buck action, synchronous freewheel (committed form)
PULSED_inductor_topup._devices: 1 high-side pMOS, 1 freewheel nMOS, 1 park nMOS, 1 inductor Ltu, 1 series R
PULSED_inductor_topup._label_defect: the row labels 3 driven gates; the integrator qgabs sums FOUR gate sources (VGTU high-side, VGFW freewheel, VGTO and VGTOP on the OUT switch). The METERING is complete -- the label undercounts, the number does not.
PULSED_inductor_topup._E_gate_convention: Q_gate*VGH, the REAL-DRIVER cost, with Q_gate MEASURED as half the |I| integral over all four gate sources. This is the number to use.

CLAMP_switched_to_ideal_source.form: RESISTIVE transmission gate to the ideal dV node, chain3's device and 20 ps window placement VERBATIM, fired at the START of the hold. The BOUNDING form: charge-conserving and therefore inefficient, but it restores the rail as hard as a supply can.
CLAMP_switched_to_ideal_source._devices: 1 nMOS + 1 pMOS transmission gate to the dV node (no inductor)

VERDICT_d.is_the_topup_cost_counted: YES, and at the CONSERVATIVE convention. Both forms meter every driven gate with Q_gate*VGH (the real-driver cost), not the ideal-PWL net energy -- which would have flattered both. The pulsed form's FOUR gates per topped bank are all in the integrator.
VERDICT_d.the_decisive_number: the PULSED top-up spends 322.2 fJ of gate drive per beat to land -1.1234 fJ in the banks. The energy landed is NEGATIVE. Its gate drive alone is 4.9x the entire two-hop transfer energy of the chain it is meant to assist.
VERDICT_d.charge_multiplication_REFUTED: the brief calls this form 'buck action, charge-multiplying'. MEASURED Qdel/Qsup = 0.058 -- it draws 160.2 fC from the supply and delivers 9.26 fC into the banks. It is a charge DIVIDER by a factor of ~16, not a multiplier.
WHAT_IS_NOT_COUNTED_in_EITHER_form: the IDEAL SUPPLY itself. ptu draws from 'VTSUP tsup 0 dv', rtu from 'VDV vdv 0 dv' -- both ideal voltage sources. The converter that would actually make that node, and its efficiency, is booked at zero in both. The committed record labels the rtu case '_ideal_source_booking: true'; the same booking is present, and unlabelled, on the ptu side.

the INDUCTOR as a physical component. Its series resistance IS modelled (RSTU = 10 ohm, so conduction loss is counted), but area, Q, self-resonance and the cost of 2 EXTRA magnetics (4 total in a 4-bank chain) are not.
JUNCTION CAPACITANCE. qal/sg13lv_compat.sp zeroes ad/as/pd/ps, so every charge and energy number here is a LOWER BOUND -- the committed record says so itself.
Cna, the switch-node capacitance, is ASSUMED at 8 fF (a DERIVED central estimate), not extracted from layout.
VERDICT_d.does_a_cost_hide_one_level_down: NO -- and this is the answer to the question I was sent to ask. The failure mode that overturned two earlier mechanisms on this campaign is not present here: the buck's two switches and their four gates ARE metered, at the conservative real-driver convention. The cost is not hidden; it is counted, and counting it is disqualifying on its own, BEFORE any settling argument.
